To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel battery control strategy that is able to minimize both Peak Charge and Energy Charge components of a Data Center's electricity bill.

1) we propose an optimal peak shaving battery control strategy for a data center when the power demands are known, and 2) we propose an efficient battery peak shaving control strategy when the power demands can only be predicted in the short term.

1) the proposed optimal control strategy for a DC with a battery can reduce its peak charge and energy charge by up to 50% compared to the case when the battery is not present, and 2) the proposed control strategy for a datacenter with a battery can significantly improve the performance of the data center in terms of peak shaving and energy charge, even when the power demand predictions of the data center are not very accurate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problem: How to efficiently charge/discharge a battery in order to minimize the DC's electricity bill?
the design of optimal control strategies for energy storage systems in DCs with the objective of peak shaving.
developing efficient control techniques that can be applied to a DC's battery for minimizing the Peak Charge component of the DC's electricity bill.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed techniques can reduce significantly the Peak and the Energy charges for the DC, while at the same time the DC can operate normally and without any interruptions.
the optimal control strategy is not always the best one in terms of cost reduction, and that a simple heuristic strategy is often sufficient to achieve the same cost reduction with less computation.
our proposed techniques can achieve significant savings in the electricity bill for a DC, while maintaining a very small battery capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed optimal peak shaving control strategies for data centers that are based on the knowledge of the DC's future power demands and that can also be applied to a battery with leakage and conversion losses.
we have developed optimal and practical control strategies for batteries in data centers that minimize the Peak and Energy components of their electricity bills.

our optimal control strategies for the battery can achieve up to 40% savings in the Peak Charge component of the electricity bill and up to 50% in the Energy Charge component of the bill, while the leakage and conversion losses of the battery are less than 1.2% of the total amount of energy that the battery stores.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal control strategy for peak shaving is not the one that minimizes the energy cost.
the proposed control strategy for the case of unknown power demand is efficient in reducing the Peak and Energy components of the electricity bill and can be implemented in practice.
a battery can help a DC to save up to 50% of its electricity bill.
